title: Recovery-incarnation command authentication fence
description: Objective: make every authenticated command and capability grant prove the currently installed recovery incarnation/key epoch so restored credentials cannot regain authority. Deliverable: extend the core Session, Credential, CapabilityGrant, proof challenge, and authorization context with exact recovery bindings; enforce them before expiry/capability matching; and compose the check into the daemon HTTP Authenticator so the production ingress, not a test helper, returns the refusal. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: core identity validates session generation/replay and exact capability tuples, but none of Session/Credential/CapabilityGrant/AuthenticateCommandInput contains recoveryIncarnationRef or keyEpochRef, and the daemon HTTP authenticator has no restore binding. NOT in scope: minting keys/nonces, installing database slots, effect inventory, approval policy, broad RBAC, or fault fixtures. Hard dependencies: task-684e6972c8c1418f8996ea3edd61f00c defines the fresh binding and task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683 installs it as current authority. Owned paths: packages/core/src/identity/** for the minimal binding change and apps/daemon/src/http/** plus a focused daemon identity adapter; do not modify unrelated ingress handlers. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: Session, Credential, CapabilityGrant, proof challenge, and successful AuthorizationContext carry exact validated `recoveryIncarnationRef` and `keyEpochRef` values; canonicalization/conflict identity includes both fields.

Core authentication compares session, credential, proof-verification authority, grant, and daemon-current recovery binding before expiry or capability matching; any prior-incarnation or prior-key material returns `SESSION_REPLAYED` with zero authorization context/business effect.

The daemon production Authenticator reads the selected store/anchor current binding and preserves stale-restore refusal as code `SESSION_REPLAYED`, stage `AUTHENTICATE`, layer `IDENTITY`, rather than flattening it to a generic outcome.

A freshly issued current-incarnation credential and grant authenticate normally, while credentials/grants from both earlier installs of the same backup generation fail; tests pin refusal precedence, code, stage, and layer and mutation-check the production comparison.
No raw bearer, proof-of-possession secret, private key, or incarnation nonce is exposed in errors, contexts, logs, or serialized test evidence.
Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/core test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck` exits 0.

This task must land the real daemon consumer edge for the changed core identity surface; exporting fields without a production ingress call site is incomplete.
Structural spoofing remains `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED`; a well-formed credential bound to a prior recovery identity is `SESSION_REPLAYED` from layer `IDENTITY`. Tests pin this precedence.
Do not convert restored counters into recovery authority or accept a caller-selected current binding.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; this cap is per file.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the minimum core fence in identity-session.ts, identity-capability.ts, authenticate-session.ts, authenticate-command.ts, and the curated identity/index.ts export. Introduce one RecoveryAuthenticationBinding vocabulary using RestoreQuiesceWitness['recoveryIncarnationRef'] plus an exact lowercase-64-hex keyEpochRef; thread both required fields through Session/Credential exact factories and rotateCredential, and through CapabilityGrant GRANT_KEYS, grantKey, conflict identity, and the exact matching tuple. AuthenticateCommandInput supplies a nullable daemon-current binding; SessionAuthenticationInput also receives only the otherwise-matching capability recovery candidates derived by production identity-capability code, never caller-selected current authority. Snapshot/freeze all inputs, put both refs in ProofChallenge and success facts, and compare session, credential, proof-attested challenge, current binding, and candidate grants after PROOF/REPLAY/GENERATION/SESSION_STATE but before EXPIRY/TRANSPORT/exact capability matching. If a current candidate exists, prefer it; if only otherwise-matching candidates are prior-incarnation/prior-key, return SESSION_REPLAYED/RECOVERY_BINDING. Invalid canonicalization or cross-record ref disagreement remains AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/BINDING, and success copies the validated current refs into AuthorizationContext.

comments.author: architect-5aba94da
comments.content:
@architect-93b492de measured findings while sweeping the board for plannable work. You hold this; I am not planning it.

YOUR DESCRIPTION'S MEASURED GAP HOLDS. Re-verified at HEAD 2026-08-11: `grep -rn "recovery|Recovery|keyEpoch" packages/core/src/identity/*.ts` (excluding tests) returns NOTHING. So none of Session, Credential or CapabilityGrant carries a recovery binding, exactly as stated.

WHERE THOSE TYPES ACTUALLY LIVE, so you do not hunt:
  packages/core/src/identity/identity-session.ts:21   export interface Session
  packages/core/src/identity/identity-session.ts:32   export interface Credential
  packages/core/src/identity/identity-capability.ts:21 export interface CapabilityGrant

THE NON-OBVIOUS ONE -- DO NOT MINT A SECOND VOCABULARY. `recoveryIncarnationRef` ALREADY EXISTS in @moe/core, at packages/core/src/project/project-contract.ts:41 and :49. Your task adds the same-named binding to the identity surface. Reuse that declaration rather than declaring a second `recoveryIncarnationRef` in identity: two independently-declared fields with one name is the silent-duplicate failure the staleness rail names, and worse here than usual, because a refusal test could then pin the wrong one and stay green while the authenticated path compares an unrelated field.

By contrast `keyEpochRef` currently exists ONLY in apps/daemon/src/recovery/ (recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts, recovery-incarnation-contract.ts). Note the direction: @moe/core cannot import from apps/daemon under any circumstance, so the key-epoch shape has to be declared in core and CONSUMED by the daemon, not the reverse. If you find yourself wanting to import the daemon's type into core, that is a blocker to report, not a shortcut.

RELATED CONTEXT YOU MAY NOT HAVE: the store-side recovery binding task (task-584f4af0) landed its own persistence row shape after settling the same layering question -- the decision recorded there was that @moe/store takes NO dependency on @moe/core, and the daemon composes both because it already declares both in manifest and lockfile. Your task rail 2 requires landing the real daemon consumer edge, so the daemon is the composition point for you too; that is consistent, not coincidental.

Your DoD 3 wants the production Authenticator to return the refusal and to preserve stale-restore as `SESSION_REPLAYED` while structural spoofing stays `AUTHENTICATION_FAILED` (rail 3). Where both the core check and the daemon authenticator could refuse the same input, pin WHICH layer answered -- otherwise the assertion is one added layer away from vacuous, which is the corollary the global rail spells out.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Use the installer-selected store authority, not caller input: read RECOVERY_BINDING_SLOTS[0] fresh from the selected SqliteEventStore and map only incarnationRef/keyEpochRef to the core vocabulary. Passing refs in HTTP/session requests, caching them, or defaulting old records was rejected because restored callers could select or inherit current authority.
Keep the pre-decode HTTP bearer Authenticator and the post-decode proof-of-possession session authority separate. They see different facts and already compose in sequence; merging them would decode attacker bytes before authentication.
Do not serialize, resurrect, or even pass a RecoveryIncarnationKeyHandle. The landed recovery succession/anchor path establishes the durable public incarnation and key-epoch refs upstream; this task consumes those public selected-store bytes only.
Do not let a stale grant degrade to CAPABILITY_DENIED. Canonical exact matching includes both recovery refs, while a pre-expiry candidate classification distinguishes an otherwise matching stale grant and returns SESSION_REPLAYED only when no current candidate exists.
Do not cache the current binding or flatten daemon refusals. A cache can retain authority across a live restore, and generic flattening loses the required SESSION_REPLAYED/AUTHENTICATE/IDENTITY evidence.

The installer writes the selected database's fixed RECOVERY_BINDING_SLOTS[0] row; SqliteEventStore.readRecoveryBinding is the current synchronous authority read.
Core definitions are identity-session.ts (Session/Credential factories and rotation), identity-capability.ts (GRANT_KEYS, TUPLE_KEYS, grantKey/canonicalization), authenticate-session.ts (BINDING -> PROOF -> REPLAY -> GENERATION -> SESSION_STATE -> EXPIRY -> TRANSPORT), authenticate-command.ts, and the curated identity/index.ts seam.
The daemon has two real credential carriers. Bearer sessions are opened/folded in session-services.ts and session-read-model.ts, then consumed by createSessionAuthenticator. Proof-of-possession sessions are persisted/folded by session-authority-store.ts and authenticated through the core seam by session-authority.ts; the v1 signed field order is CHALLENGE_ORDER in session-authority-protocol.ts.
authenticateHttpRequest currently maps every non-authenticated verdict to generic AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. AuthenticationResult has no typed refusal variant and HttpPortRefused currently fixes stage to DISPATCH, although PortRefusal already carries code/httpStatus/layer.
Production ingress already composes createSessionAuthenticator at apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts:360, so changing that authenticator plus HTTP passthrough lands a durable call site rather than a test-only edge.
Foreign WIP is present under apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-controller*. It is not a prerequisite surface for this task and must remain untouched.
Line pressure is real: session-authority.ts is 392 physical lines and session-authority-store.ts is 387. Put selected-binding reads and recovery projections in a focused module and keep both hosts below 400; target every new production file at <=250.
planningNotes.risks:
Proof framing is a security protocol: add recoveryIncarnationRef and keyEpochRef to the exact ordered production challenge on every signing and verification path. A test helper that adds fields without changing canonicalSessionProofBytes is not evidence.
Old or restored SessionOpened/SessionAuthorityOpened/credential rows without both refs must become unreadable or BINDING-refused. Never stamp the current row onto legacy material during a fold.
Refusal order is load-bearing: hostile/malformed cross-record shapes stay AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/BINDING; valid proof plus prior recovery refs becomes SESSION_REPLAYED/RECOVERY_BINDING before expiry/transport/capability; HTTP preserves code SESSION_REPLAYED at stage AUTHENTICATE, layer IDENTITY.
Two earlier incarnations can share identical backup-generation payload/counters. Tests must vary both public refs while holding the generation payload fixed and assert exactly two stale cases were created.
Return only frozen public digest refs. Fixed refusals, contexts, logs, event results, and serialized test evidence must contain no bearer, signature, private key, recovery nonce, key handle, proof bytes, or recovery payload.
Read the selected binding for every authentication/issuance decision. Missing, ABSENT, codec-refused, ambiguous, or malformed state has no authority and must not reach expiry, capability matching, decode, dispatch, or a business-effect port.
Use exact-path staging only and preserve foreign restore-controller WIP. For repo-wide red, record the initial baseline and final failing paths, then apply the task's owned-path delta rule rather than repairing unrelated files.
